$comment: Copyleft components that ship. Each entry is a decision with its reason, not a mute button: scripts/licensing/third-party-notices.mjs fails when one is missing, or when its placement no longer matches the build. An entry marked `paths: false` also claims the app can never reach it; the script re-reads the render path and fails as soon as that claim stops being true.

reasons.name: elkjs
reasons.does: The ELK layout engine mermaid uses for `layout: elk` diagrams
reasons.reason: Kept, not dropped. EPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: unmodified (source at github.com/kieler/elkjs) as a binary inside a GPL-3.0-or-later work, it asks only that the source stay available, which a public build already satisfies. It rides in mermaid's diagram chunk and nothing in this app reaches it: `src/lib/ui/mermaid.ts` initializes mermaid with `layout: 'dagre'`, and `mermaidText()` in `src/lib/pulls/pullGraph.ts` encodes `#`, `%` and `<` out of every title, branch and label, so repository content, model output and PR titles cannot open a `%%{init}%%` directive or a `flowchart-elk` diagram. Dropping it would cost `flowchart-elk` rendering for 1.4 MB nobody downloads by default.

reasons.name: node-liblzma
reasons.does: liblzma binding that just-bash (@cloudflare/computer) uses for .tar.xz archives
reasons.reason: Never bundled: the npm bin binding cannot be built for Workers, so the worker requires it at runtime and gets nothing, leaving `.tar.xz` unsupported. Should a deployment need that archive format, LGPL-3.0 only requires keeping the library replaceable, so ship it next to the build rather than as part of it.
